A 49-year-old male patient comes to your clinic reporting a two-month history of abdominal bloating,
early satiety, and occasional vomiting with large meals. His diarrhea has recently become more severe,
significantly impacting his quality of life. His medical history includes recent antibiotic use for an ear
infection and dietary changes to low-fat dairy products and reduced meat consumption. Physical
examination reveals a temperature of 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure 197/91 mmHg, pulse 68/min,
respiratory rate 15/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Previous laboratory results show a

hemoglobin A1c of 13%. What is the most appropriate treatment for this patient's diarrhea? Answer
Choices: (A) Octreotide (B) Metoclopramide (C) Better glycemic control (D) Dietary modification with
low FODMAP diet (E) Rifaximin (F) Cholestyramine (G) Loperamide (H) Pancreatic enzyme
replacement (I) Probiotics (J) Lactase enzyme supplements
 A. Loperamide
B. Pancreatic enzyme replacement
